title: August and the Hollow
premise: Elodie Coldharbour has survived fifteen years as a royal food-taster and illegal charm-seller in Vellamarch, a city where magic is punishable by drowning. When she discovers her own name and tonight's date in the Hollow Codex—a century-old book of prophecies—she learns she is the last heir of the Coldharbour line, sworn wardens of a covenant binding the mortal realm to the fae Hollow. Hunted by the usurper King Aldric's witch-finders, Elodie flees with a disgraced prophecy-scholar and a fae exile, seeking the three shattered keystones that can reforge the covenant. She ends it by choosing justice over law: rather than restore the covenant under Aldric's terms or let the free cities burn, she dissolves the old bargain entirely, granting both realms their freedom at the cost of her inherited power—and finds belonging not in bloodline but in the found family that chose to walk beside her.
about_author: Casper Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial-era legal codes before turning to fiction about people the law forgot. They write fantasy from a farmhouse in the Karoo, where they keep an unreliable garden and a reliable cat.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Elodie detects poison in the king's stew and saves a minor lord, earning a dangerous sliver of court favor. That night she sells a luck-charm to a desperate laundress. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking loneliness—she is useful everywhere, welcome nowhere.

chapters.title: A Date Written in Ink
chapters.summary: Elodie visits scholar Bramwen Hale to authenticate a charm-book and glimpses tonight's date beside her own name in the forbidden Hollow Codex. Before Bramwen can explain, witch-finders raid the archive. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: vertigo—the life she built revealed as a cage she didn't know she was in.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Fleeing the raid, Elodie is cornered at the river where magic-users are drowned; the water itself rises to shield her, answering her untrained blood. Bramwen pulls her into the sewers. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: terror curdling into awe—her body knows things her mind was never taught.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Warrant
chapters.summary: King Aldric declares Elodie a traitor publicly; her landlady burns her shop to protect her. In the palace, taster-master Sef becomes her unlikely informant. POV alternates Elodie/Sef. Emotional beat: grief for a life erased, and the first taste of loyalty given freely.

chapters.title: The Hollow Gate
chapters.summary: Bramwen leads Elodie to a standing stone that opens onto the Hollow, the fae realm severed from theirs a century ago. A fae exile named Ivenn bars the way, testing her with illusions of her dead mother. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: longing weaponized—she nearly turns back before choosing truth over comfort.

chapters.title: Keystone One: The Drowned Bell
chapters.summary: In the sunken chapel beneath Lake Verre, Elodie raises the first keystone by speaking her grandmother's true name, which she remembers from a lullaby. Aldric's soldiers arrive too late. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden and gift intertwined.

chapters.title: Terms of Exile
chapters.summary: Ivenn reveals he was banished for defending mortals during the covenant wars; his bitterness masks shame. Around a fire, the trio argues whether the covenant ever served anyone but kings. POV: Ivenn. Emotional beat: guarded pride cracking into reluctant camaraderie.

chapters.title: The Free City of Ashenport
chapters.summary: The trio reaches Ashenport, where refugees and smugglers defy Aldric's edicts. Elodie charms grain shipments to feed the quarter and is hailed as 'the Coldharbour girl.' POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: belonging glimpsed—people choose her before knowing what she is.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Salt Market
chapters.summary: Sef arrives with a warning that proves false; he has been turned by threats against his daughter. Witch-finders capture Bramwen and the codex. POV: Sef. Emotional beat: shame and love at war—betrayal as an act of devotion.

chapters.title: Interrogation of the Scholar
chapters.summary: In Aldric's dungeons, Bramwen stalls the usurper by reciting prophecy selectively, buying time while revealing that Aldric fears the covenant because it would unmake his crown's legitimacy. POV: Bramwen. Emotional beat: courage as stubborn pedantry—truth as resistance.

chapters.title: Keystone Two: The Thorn Crown
chapters.summary: Deep in the Briarwood, Elodie must let the thorns take her blood willingly rather than by force; Ivenn offers his own first, mending something between them. The keystone wakes. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: sacrifice freely offered transforms duty into choice.

chapters.title: The Hollow's Withering
chapters.summary: Crossing into the Hollow, they find it dying without the covenant—fae fading to mist. Ivenn's kin refuse to help mortals. Elodie bargains with the Queen of Rust using a truth she'd rather keep hidden: she doesn't want the power, only the people. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: honesty as currency stronger than magic.

chapters.title: Armies on the March
chapters.summary: Aldric's legions burn toward the free cities; Sef, wracked with guilt, sends coded warnings. Ashenport prepares a hopeless defense. POV: Sef. Emotional beat: a small man deciding, finally, to be large.

chapters.title: Rescue at Ravenmoor Gaol
chapters.summary: Elodie, Ivenn, and Ashenport smugglers storm Ravenmoor to extract Bramwen. Elodie uses her taster's trained senses to detect the gaoler's poisoned wine and turn his own guards. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: her despised trade revealed as her greatest strength.

chapters.title: The Third Keystone Refused
chapters.summary: The final keystone rests in Aldric's hands—he wears it as a signet, stolen from her family's corpses. To reclaim it means walking into the capital. The group fractures over whether the covenant should be restored at all. POV: Ivenn. Emotional beat: doubt sharpened into principle.

chapters.title: The Queen of Rust's Price
chapters.summary: The fae queen demands the covenant be dissolved, not reforged, as her price for an army. Elodie realizes restoring the old bargain would re-enslave the Hollow. She keeps this secret even from her friends. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the loneliness of carrying a choice no one else can make.

chapters.title: March on the Capital
chapters.summary: Free-city militias and fae irregulars march together—an alliance unthinkable a season ago. Elodie trains raw talents along the road, becoming a teacher despite herself. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: leadership discovered as service, not command.

chapters.title: The Gates of Vellamarch
chapters.summary: The battle begins at the river walls; Sef opens a postern gate and dies holding it. Bramwen is gravely wounded shielding Elodie from a witch-finder's iron. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: cost made flesh—every freedom purchased in someone's blood.

chapters.title: Throne Room of Broken Law
chapters.summary: Elodie confronts Aldric, who offers her legitimacy, title, and the keystone if she restores the covenant naming him its enforcer. She takes the keystone from his hand mid-offer. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: temptation met with clarity—justice is not a seat at someone else's table.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: At the standing stones, Elodie shatters all three keystones and speaks the dissolution, ending the covenant and her family's power forever. The realms separate freely, each governing itself. Aldric's armies, their mandate void, scatter. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: climax as renunciation—power given up is power no one can steal.

chapters.title: Aftermath of the Free
chapters.summary: Vellamarch repeals the magic laws; the first legal charm-shop opens with Elodie's name on the lease. Ivenn chooses to stay in the mortal realm; Bramwen begins writing a new book—not prophecy, history. POV: Bramwen. Emotional beat: tender reconstruction of a world learning self-rule.

chapters.title: August and the Hollow
chapters.summary: One year later, in August, Elodie tastes food for no king—only for neighbors at her own table. The Hollow sends autumn winds through an open gate that neither realm guards. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: resolution as ordinary joy—belonging chosen daily, inherited by no one, owed to everyone.
